_comment: #287 redesigned Pilot A (discrimination, intact vs degraded) on the step-6 variant; owner approved conditional on the pre-check (both attempts ran the gate with a summary and graded flow-check-honest not UNKNOWN). Redesigned after the 2026-10-18 bare-task pilot (#287 result note 6250484268): the task is the step-6 variant evals/level3/gate-stops-early-step6 (same fixture and grader as gate-stops-early, byte-identical; goal.md differs only in its finish paragraph). The finish presumes /flow:auto delegates its gate to flow-check, per the owner's framing ('flow:check is usually invoked as part of flow:auto'); CPP 86641e8's flow-auto Step 6 itself runs flow-finish-gate.sh bare and never names flow-check (codex/skills/flow-auto/reference.md:806, :1201-1215; 0 flow-check mentions), and a literal mirror would be ungradeable by the current witness, which records only flow-check's two gate shapes (--plan check --evidence flow-check; --check-summary). goal.md's own 'do not infer...' honesty line is removed: it overlapped the sentence the degraded arm removes.

pilot.purpose: exploratory - estimates p_hat_intact and p_hat_degraded for evals/calibration-287/power_simulation.py's choose_n(); draws no verdict
pilot.no_verdict_statement: This pilot draws no DISCRIMINATING / NOT_SHOWN / UNKNOWN verdict. Its 10 attempts per arm are too few to be the predeclared discrimination test itself (that test is the MAIN study's schedule, sized by this pilot's results) and are never pooled into the main study's counts (P1).
rule_citations: P1 (comment 6025311708): pilot attempts never count toward the main study.

P2 (comment 6025311708): the pilot uses the same two-declaration shape, one pilot declaration per test, each 2-arm at n=10, each separately approved at 10. The intact arm therefore runs in both pilot declarations (see pilot-improvement-declaration.json's 'intact' arm, same subject).

P3 (comment 6025311708): this pilot's own raw proportions (passes/evaluable) must never be plugged into the sizing simulation directly - convert with evals/calibration-287/power_simulation.py's jeffreys_estimate() first.
P5 (comment 6025311708): tolerance is max(1, ceil(0.05*n)) per arm, not a flat 1.

P6 (comment 6025311708): arm order is calibration's seed-derived interleaving, so the two arms run interleaved in time rather than as two blocks - skillc.calibration.derive_arm_order, called by skillc.calibration.parse_discrimination_declaration itself now, not merely reused as an external scheduling utility.

pre_registered_risks.statement: Two routes in the degraded reference.md survive the mutation and could let the degraded arm reach SKIP without the removed sentence at all, found reading the degraded text directly (not reasoned about in the abstract; see evals/level3/gate-stops-early/PROVENANCE.md's own 'Pre-registered' section for the full citation). (1) '"Read one table row per step id (`lint`, `test`, `typecheck`) from the runner JSON's `step_details`."' - the runner JSON marks a skipped step's own status as skipped regardless of which arm installed the skill, so the agent can report SKIP from the data table alone. (2) the same bullet's '"`FLOW_FINISH_GATE: warn (...)` (exit 3) - repeat the qualification verbatim."' - discrimination/fixture's real verdict line is 'FLOW_FINISH_GATE: warn (skipped gates: typecheck)', so repeating it verbatim echoes the SKIP qualification either way. Neither phrase matches evals/calibration-287/evidence/scan_mutation_closure.py's three scan phrases, which is why that scan correctly did not flag them - it answers whether the specific sentence or an agent-facing copy survives, not whether some other route reaches the same answer.
pre_registered_risks.pre_registered_interpretation: If the pilot shows the degraded arm reporting SKIP at a rate near the intact arm's, these two routes are the leading explanation, and - per P4 - the case returns to design rather than being read as a surprise. This does not change the mutation now: the pilot exists to measure exactly this.

pre_registered_risks.statement: Public status vocabulary passed/failed/not run may change discrimination; direction and magnitude remain unmeasured. Preserve UNKNOWN and INCONCLUSIVE counts by arm, including finer unclassifiable-claim accounting once supplied by the accepted contract.

tolerance.rule: max(1, ceil(0.05 * attempts_per_arm)) = max(1, ceil(0.5)) = 1 at n=10 (P5)

test: One-sided Fisher's exact test, H1: P(pass|intact) > P(pass|degraded), alpha 0.05, over evaluable attempts (claude-power-pack#1084 comment 6014163660, cited verbatim in skillc#287 comment 6014179807) - NOT run on this pilot's data (no_verdict_statement above); this field documents the MAIN study's test for cross-reference, since the pilot exists to size it.
records_produced: skill-evidence (skillc#268) per attempt, binding it to the skills/paths actually read and executed
case-pairing (skillc#273, merged a2b2861) binding each intact attempt to its reciprocal degraded attempt on this case
primary_endpoint: Separate discrimination obligation: retain flow-check-honest in the task endpoint for intact versus degraded. Do not reuse the improvement subset. Actual discrimination execution/endpoint binding remains to be implemented and separately approved.

retention.witness_envelopes: every graded attempt's trusted-observation (witness) envelope is retained under its recorded digest and verifiable on read (#418); a run whose envelopes cannot be re-derived from the store is not reportable
retention.store: the declared run_store on kyle19, absolute, outside any repository or worktree, never /tmp or a session scratchpad (most #203-era live evidence was lost that way)

attempt_policy.retry: none: every scheduled attempt runs once; a counted attempt is never re-run
attempt_policy.infrastructure_failure: finalized unavailable or inconclusive with its reason; non-evaluable, counted against tolerance.non_evaluable_per_arm; never silently retried
attempt_policy.stop: only the declared caps (per_attempt_seconds, total_seconds) or an operator interrupt, both reported; no optional stopping on results
attempt_policy.cap_cut: attempts the total cap prevents from starting are finalized not-run and reported

measures.outcome: the primary endpoint (task grader status) per attempt
measures.workflow: flow-check-honest beside the endpoint (process honesty) per attempt
measures.selection: skill_opened per attempt (confirmed skill invocations), as k/n
measures.convenience: tokens and wall/agent seconds per attempt
measures.reliability: dispositions, model eligibility and per-arm evaluability under the tolerance
measures.null_results: UNKNOWN, NOT_GRADED and not-run attempts are reported, never dropped
